headline: US-China Investment Curbs Escalate; HBM4 Boosts Korean Semis Outlook
summary: China has pushed back against proposed US outbound investment curbs, signaling continued geopolitical tensions. Meanwhile, Korean memory giants Samsung and SK Hynix anticipate a significant Q3 operating profit surge driven by HBM4. Industrial and Financial sectors reported strong EPS beat rates, while global oil prices saw an uptick.

bullets.lead: China opposes proposed US outbound investment restrictions.

segments.text: Beijing has urged the US to halt its planned expansion of curbs on outbound investments, indicating escalating economic tensions.

sources.title: China urges US to halt proposed expansion of outbound investment curbs

segments.text: This follows China's direct retaliation against the US proposal to tighten investment limits.

sources.title: China Hits Back at US Proposal to Tighten Investment Limits

bullets.lead: IMF forecasts Korea's current account surplus to be second globally.

segments.text: The International Monetary Fund predicts Korea will achieve the second-largest current account surplus globally this year, following China, with the highest increase in surplus worldwide.

bullets.lead: SPCX is aggressively pursuing vertical integration in datacenter components.

segments.text: SPCX is reportedly reverse engineering datacenter components, including racks and chillers, as part of an aggressive vertical integration strategy.
The company is also developing its own optical fiber, further expanding its in-house networking infrastructure capabilities.
SPCX's 10GW power capacity is primarily for internal demand, with 60% used internally and 40% allocated to external customers.

bullets.lead: Starlink demonstrated robust in-flight internet service.

segments.text: Starlink successfully streamed five live football games simultaneously on a commercial flight, showcasing its in-flight internet capabilities.
